'''''Asparagus densiflorus''''' (among several species colloquially called  '''asparagus ferns'''; no relation to actual [[fern]]s), or the '''foxtail fern (asparagus)''' or '''plume fern''', is a variable, [[evergreen]]-[[perennial plant]] related to cultivated, edible [[asparagus]].

It is [[native plant|native]] to [[southern Africa]], from [[Mozambique]] to [[South Africa]], but is widely cultivated.<ref name=POWO_531072-1/>

==Related species==
Foxtail asparagus is part of a group of similar-looking and related ''[[Asparagus (genus)|Asparagus]]'' species native to Africa, including ''[[Asparagus aethiopicus]]'' ("Sprenger's asparagus"), ''A. confertus'' and ''[[Asparagus krebsianus|A. krebsianus]]''.<ref>{{cite journal|author=Maria F Norup|author2= Gitte Petersen |author3= Sandie Burrows|author4= Yanis Bouchenak-Khelladi|author5= Jim Leebens-Mack|author6= J Chris Pires|author7= H Peter Linder|author8= Ole Seberg|year=2015|title=Evolution of Asparagus L. (Asparagaceae): Out-of-South-Africa and multiple origins of sexual dimorphism|journal=Molecular Phylogenetics and Evolution|volume=92|pages=25–44|doi= 10.1016/j.ympev.2015.06.002 |pmid= 26079131 |bibcode= 2015MolPE..92...25N }}</ref> It is mainly found in rocky open forest, savanna thickets and coastal regions of southeastern South Africa.<ref>{{cite web |title=''Asparagus densiflorus'' |url=https://www.missouribotanicalgarden.org/PlantFinder/PlantFinderDetails.aspx?kempercode=b578 |publisher=[[Missouri Botanical Garden]] |access-date=30 April 2026}}</ref> ''Asparagus densiflorus'' has been occasionally confused with ''[[Asparagus aethiopicus]]''—a different, spikier, more rambling and pendant species<ref name="pza.sanbi.org">{{cite web | url=https://pza.sanbi.org/asparagus-aethiopicus | title=''Asparagus aethiopicus'' {{!}} PlantZAfrica }}</ref><ref>{{cite book|url=http://www.efloras.org/florataxon.aspx?flora_id=1&taxon_id=242101423|volume=26|pages= 213, 214|chapter=''Asparagus aethiopicus''|title=Flora of North America|access-date=2009-07-29}}</ref><ref name=POWO_531072-1/>—thus some sources provide incorrect information in reference to ''A. densiflorus''. The plant formerly often grown as ''A. densiflorus'' var. 'Sprengeri' is, simply, ''A. densiflorus''.<ref>{{cite web | url=https://pza.sanbi.org/asparagus-densiflorus | title=''Asparagus densiflorus'' {{!}} PlantZAfrica }}</ref><ref name="pza.sanbi.org" /> Furthermore, the species known as ''A. densiflorus'' var. 'Meyersii' remains ''A. densiflorus'', as well.

As a whole, the ''Asparagus'' genera is part of a larger botanical order, the [[Asparagales]], which groups together other related plant [[Family (taxonomy)|families]] such as the [[agave]]s, [[cordyline]]s, [[Dracaena (plant)|dracaenas]], [[Orchidaceae|orchids]], [[Beaucarnea|ponytail palms]], [[Sansevieria|snake]] and [[Chlorophytum|spider plants]], and [[yucca]]s (Joshua trees).

==Distribution==
''Asparagus densiflorus'' is native to the [[Cape Provinces]], [[KwaZulu-Natal]] and the [[Northern Provinces]] in South Africa, [[Eswatini]] (Swaziland) and the [[Inhaca Island]]s of Mozambique.<ref name=POWO_531072-1/>

==Cultivation==
As it cannot tolerate frost, in [[temperate]] regions ''A.densiflorus'' is usually grown under glass. Numerous [[cultivars]] have been developed, of which the compact form 'Meyersii' has gained the [[Royal Horticultural Society]]'s [[Award of Garden Merit]].<ref>{{cite web|title=RHS Plant Selector - ''Asparagus densiflorus'' 'Myersii'|url=
https://www.rhs.org.uk/Plants/28198/Asparagus-densiflorus-Myersii/Details|access-date=15 April 2020}}</ref> Its dense {{cvt|50|cm}} plumes of foliage are especially valued in [[flower arranging]].
